# Copilot instructions — Codescribe

`@AGENTS.md` is the authoritative per-repo contract (thrones of authority, worker
embargo, shared compile cache, release cadence). This file adds what Copilot gets
wrong most often: commit provenance, the two remotes, merge conflicts and the
shared working tree. When this file and `AGENTS.md` disagree, `AGENTS.md` wins.

## Commit messages — the provenance gate

Every commit is checked by `scripts/commit-msg-provenance.sh` (pre-commit, stage
`commit-msg`). A commit whose first line does not match is rejected. Never work
around the gate with `--no-verify`; fix the message instead.

First line, exactly one of:

- `[copilot/vc-<workflow>] <what changed>` — your own work. `copilot` is your
  agent name; never borrow `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `grok` or `junie`. Use a
  real workflow slug: `vc-workflow` (default), `vc-justdo`, `vc-marbles`,
  `vc-polish`, `vc-review`. Lowercase agent, lowercase slug, one space after `]`.
- `Merge …` — a merge commit (see conflicts below).
- `Revert "<original first line>"` — a revert keeps the provenance of what it reverts.

Body: bullet points, never empty, in English. State what changed and why; name
the gate you ran (`make check`, `make verify`, `make test-swift`, targeted tests).

Trailers, as the last lines of the body:

```
Authored-By: copilot <agents@vetcoders.io>
```

Rules for trailers:

- One `Authored-By` line per agent that actually wrote the code; for your own
  commits that is exactly `copilot`.
- Keep every existing `Authored-By` trailer when you amend, squash, cherry-pick or
  rebase someone else's commit, and keep their first line. You do not inherit or
  overwrite another agent's provenance.
- Never add `Co-Authored-By`, `Reviewed-By`, `Signed-off-by`, "Generated by",
  or vendor footers such as `noreply@github.com` or `copilot@github.com`.
- Commit messages, PR titles and PR bodies are written in English only.

Example of a complete message:

```
[copilot/vc-workflow] settings: keep the model chip label when the sidebar collapses

- The chip lost its accessibility label on collapse; the label is now bound to the row, not the width
- make test-swift -only-testing:CodescribeTests/SettingsChromeContractTests green

Authored-By: copilot <agents@vetcoders.io>
```

## Two remotes: fast-forward first

The integration branch moves on two remotes: `origin` (GitHub) and the build
host remote (`<build-remote>` below; `git remote -v` shows its name in your checkout). Founder's rule, 2026-10-13: pull `--ff-only` first; when a
fast-forward is impossible, either `--rebase` or a `--no-ff` merge. Rewritten
hashes of your own unpushed commits are not a problem. Never `--force` over a
remote branch.

```
git pull <build-remote> <branch> --ff-only || git pull <build-remote> <branch> --rebase
git push origin <branch>
```

A rebase keeps every incoming commit's title, body and trailers untouched. A
merge commit's first line starts with `Merge ` and its body lists each
conflicted file and how it was resolved.

## Merge conflicts

- Resolve by reading both sides' intent. Never take `--ours` or `--theirs`
  wholesale, never drop a hunk because it is easier, never leave conflict markers
  (`check-merge-conflict` in pre-commit blocks them).
- Keep the incoming commits exactly as they are (titles, bodies, trailers). The
  resolution lives in the merge commit or in the rebased commit it belongs to. If
  you need a separate commit for the resolution, it carries your own tag and
  trailer (`[copilot/vc-workflow] fix: resolve …`, `Authored-By: copilot …`);
  never an empty or untagged message, never an amend of someone else's commit.
- Do not hand-edit generated files to resolve a conflict; regenerate them:
  - `macos/Codescribe/Resources/Localization/Localizable.xcstrings`:
    `make l10n-build`, then `L10N_DERIVED=macos/build/l10n make l10n-sync`,
    then `make verify-l10n-catalog`. Commit the catalog with the Swift change.
  - `macos/Codescribe/Bridge/codescribe_ffi.swift`, `codescribe_ffiFFI.h`:
    `make app-bindings`.
- After resolving, run the gate that covers the touched surface before committing
  (`make check` for Rust, `make test-swift` for Swift, the Python test file under
  `scripts/tests/` for bus scripts). A conflict resolution that was not built is not
  resolved.
- Never rewrite published history: no `--force`, no `--force-with-lease` on a
  branch you did not create, no `reset --hard`, no interactive rebase, no deleting
  branches or tags, no `stash drop`. Pushing the branch you were given
  fast-forward is fine; merging into `main` is the Founder's button.

## Shared working tree

Several agents and the Founder work in the same checkout and on the same branch.

- A dirty worktree is usually someone else's work in progress. Never
  `git checkout -- <file>`, `git stash`, `git clean` or revert files you did not
  change. Commit only your own paths: `git commit -- <paths>`.
- Pull before you commit; push fast-forward after each coherent cut.
- Do not run `make install-app`, restart the app, clear `target/` or
  `macos/build/` or run cleanup while another build is active.
- Never commit `.env*`, credentials, or anything under `~/.codescribe`. Do not
  edit the operator prompts (`DEFAULT_ASSISTIVE_PROMPT`, `~/.codescribe/prompts/*`).

## Code and vocabulary

- Rust 2024 edition; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is
  the bar. Swift 6 strict concurrency, warnings are errors, no warning suppressors.
- Swift copy changed (`Text`, `String(localized:)`, `comment:`)? Run the catalog
  recipe above and commit `Localizable.xcstrings` in the same commit; CI runs
  `verify-l10n-sync` and goes red otherwise. A placeholder or label passed to
  AppKit as a plain `String` is invisible to the extractor and loses its Polish.
- Do not introduce the words `shim`, `compat`, `legacy`, `adapter-for-old`,
  `fallback-to-previous`, `bridge-until` or `TODO remove` in code, diffs or
  commits. One throne per authority: replace a competing implementation, never wrap it.
- Interface copy goes through `String(localized:)` with a Polish translation in the
  catalog; the product is spelled `Codescribe`, the framework `Vibecrafted`.
- The only signature allowed in code and acknowledgements:
  `𝚅𝚒𝚋𝚎𝚌𝚛𝚊𝚏𝚝𝚎𝚍. with AI Agents by Vetcoders (c)2024-2026 LibraxisAI`.

## When dispatched as a worker on the STT engine

The worker embargo in `AGENTS.md` applies: write the code, hand over the commit
and the list of uncertainties, do not compile, do not run tests, do not install.
The named integrator runs the gates.
